name: Fingolimod
route_note: Once-daily oral capsule; first-dose cardiac monitoring required.
originator: Kyoto University (Tetsuro Fujita), Yoshitomi Pharmaceutical and Taito; developed by Novartis

discovery.by: Tetsuro Fujita and colleagues, Kyoto University
discovery.note: Synthesised by simplifying the structure of myriocin, an immunosuppressive metabolite of the fungus Isaria sinclairii used in traditional Chinese medicine.

tagline: First oral multiple sclerosis therapy, derived from a fungal metabolite
summary: Fingolimod was the first oral disease-modifying therapy for relapsing multiple sclerosis. It traps lymphocytes in lymph nodes by modulating S1P receptors, preventing them from entering the central nervous system.
mechanism: Fingolimod is phosphorylated by sphingosine kinase 2 to fingolimod-phosphate, which binds S1P receptors. On lymphocytes it initially activates and then causes internalisation and degradation of S1P1, making cells unresponsive to the S1P gradient that guides their exit from lymph nodes.

Naive and central memory T cells are therefore retained in lymphoid tissue, lowering circulating lymphocytes and autoreactive cell entry into the brain. Effects on S1P receptors in heart muscle cause transient bradycardia after the first dose.
uses: Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis in adults and children aged 10 and older

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: FTY720 is synthesised in Japan as a myriocin derivative.

history.title: Novartis licence
history.detail: Novartis licenses the compound, initially for transplant immunosuppression.

history.title: FREEDOMS, TRANSFORMS and approval
history.detail: Phase 3 trials (NEJM) show relapse reduction versus placebo and interferon beta-1a; the FDA approves Gilenya in September.

history.title: Paediatric approval
history.detail: Fingolimod becomes the first DMT approved for paediatric MS in the US.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic fingolimod launches in the US after patent litigation.

pk.metabolism: phosphorylation by sphingosine kinase; oxidation mainly by CYP4F2

serious: Serious infections including cryptococcal meningitis, herpes and PML

facts: Myriocin, fingolimod's parent compound, comes from a fungus related to Cordyceps, which grows on insect larvae.
